messages.author: 38e260fc5780b4d6
messages.subject: speeding up a space-time model?
parts:
Hi again Stan team,

I've been running a spatio-temporal model using Stan. The model is written as a predictive process where we sample at knots throughout the domain. The smooth spatial process (the vegetation) is then linked to count data (pollen) through a dirichlet multinomial process. I would like to run the model for a large spatial domain, but things are quite slow (2 days and still on first iteration). Currently I am subdiving the domain so I can get results, but this is not ideal. The attached data is for one of these sub-domains that has about ~3000 parameters (6 different spatial processes with about 50 knots each, times the number of times which is about 10). There are some matrices that are quite large (16000000 entries), that get built and multiplied, but I didn't think this was huge. 

Sampler seems to do well, but it takes a (very) long time. I'm looking for ways to speed this up, but am not quite sure where the bottle-neck is. When I try to profile, the model seems to spend a lot of time in the agrad namespace - is this the auto-diff computing the gradient? I can write down my gradient by hand, and suspect that using this will make things faster, but I see a previous post on the users list (see: https://groups.google.com/forum/#!searchin/stan-users/gradient/stan-users/RqT5SZFn9Ks/XzmpEJvDnGQJ) which seems to suggest that it's more complicated than writing down the gradient and modifying the C++ code. I'm not quite sure what Bob means when he refers to log Jacobian determinant adjustments...

Any thoughts on adjustments I could make to speed things up, or ideas about where the bottle-neck is? 

Cheers, 
Andria

messages.author: 2a7f346506a3e9ff
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] speeding up a space-time model?
parts:
What you likely need is the multi_gp distribution that I implemented a few months back.  It's been pending someone having the time to write some more unit tests.  You can follow the pull request here: https://github.com/stan-dev/stan/pull/350 

Of more immediate practical note here are a few tips:
- inverse() is *very* inefficient in Stan right now.  It's also generally a bad idea to explicitly compute the inverse of a matrix unless you absolutely have to.  I expect that if you can rewrite your model without inverse it would probably be faster.
- As strange as it sounds, it's almost always faster to create a large vector full of entries and then call sum(vec) than looping to sum the entries on the fly.
- C_t doesn't depend on k at all, so it would be much faster to construct it (and C_t_inv if you really need it) outside of the loop over k.  That way it's only done once.

Cheers,
Marcus

Hi Lukio,

I don't remember seeing Andria on the list for a while.

If I recall correctly, she:
1. Calculated the gradient by hand, correctly
2. Generated c++ using the Stan compiler, stanc, in CmdStan
3. Replaced the autodiff code with a function that returns both the function value and the gradients. I believe she was using a parallelization package for the gradient calculation. 
4. Compiled that under CmdStan.

Daniel

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: speeding up a space-time model?
parts:
If you only get 4 iterations in 2 days, you're not going to get
far enough to run. Is there a way to initialize to reasonable
parameter values? Or a way to reparameterize the model? Going to
a C++ rewrite is pretty extreme, but possible in Stan if you can
optimize the derivative calculations --- it won't make sampling
any more efficient, just the calculations of the log density and
derivatives.

- Bob
